is_anopheles.evidence: Tested Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes collected from field breeding sites in Nigeria (pages 1-3).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study evaluates insecticide susceptibility using WHO bioassays and PBO synergist tests, but does not genotype any target insecticide-resistance markers.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype counts or marker allele frequencies are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquito larvae and pupae were collected from field breeding sites in Ute Okpu, Umunede, and Akumazi in Delta State, Nigeria (page 2).

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary empirical study reporting bioassay and synergist results on field-collected mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: Ute Okpu (6.1476°N, 6.2907°E), Umunede (6.2582°N, 6.3067°E), and Akumazi (6.2554°N, 6.3253°E), Delta State, Nigeria (page 2).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: The paper does not explicitly state the specific year(s) of mosquito collection.

duplicate_risk.evidence: No indication of overlap or reuse of previously published datasets.

supplement.evidence: No supplementary files are required as no marker genotyping was performed.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated the susceptibility of field-collected Anopheles gambiae, Culex quinquefasciatus, and Aedes albopictus from Delta State, Nigeria to lambda-cyhalothrin (0.05%) and DDT (4%) using WHO tube bioassays and PBO synergist assays. Anopheles gambiae showed resistance to both insecticides, which was partially or fully restored with PBO pre-exposure. No molecular target marker genotyping was conducted.
